name: Reem
story_so_far: After our ship sank in a storm, I washed up on this island with Noura, Faisal, Salem, and Khalid. Khalid, our leader, died of hunger and exhaustion on Day 8. Since then, injuries have crippled us: my ankle gave out on Day 8, Salem twisted his on Day 10, and Faisal's injury became debilitating on Day 12. For a long time, I was helpless, watching Noura and Faisal struggle to feed us. However, my ankle has since improved, allowing me to venture into the jungle. Today, I was able to gather food and wood, contributing to our dwindling supplies alongside Noura and Salem. We are a group of broken people, struggling against hunger and injury, but we are still fighting.

Noura.note: She is incredibly resilient and continues to gather food even when things look hopeless.

Faisal.note: He worked through immense pain for so long, but now his injury has sidelined him.

Salem.note: He is our hunter, and seeing him active in the jungle today gives me some hope for our food supply.

Khalid.note: His death left a massive void in our leadership that no one has been able to fill.

plans: I intend to head back into the jungle tomorrow to gather more wood and food, as our supplies are still quite low and we need to prepare for more nights like this.

diary.text: Everything feels so surreal. I woke up on this beach exhausted and alone, and now I'm sharing it with strangers. Khalid seems to be trying to take charge, which is good, but I'm still terrified. At least we managed to find some food today. I hope we can find a way home soon.

Today was harder than yesterday. Noura is hurt; she woke up with a badly twisted ankle and can't help us at all. It's worrying to see someone incapacitated when we are already so vulnerable. Khalid and Salem went into the jungle again, and Faisal went to the reef. I managed to find one small bit of food near the camp, but it's getting harder to find things. I just hope everyone stays safe out there.

Today felt a bit more productive, but the uncertainty is still heavy. Noura managed to find a little food despite her ankle, which was a relief. I spent my morning searching near the camp, but it's clearly getting harder to find anything around here. Faisal and Salem are still out exploring or hunting, and I find myself constantly waiting for them to return with news. I'm exhausted, and I just hope tomorrow brings more certainties.

Today was a strange mix of relief and new worry. I managed to find a decent amount of food at the reef, which makes me feel a little less anxious about our survival. However, seeing Khalid wake up with a badly twisted ankle was a shock; he's been such a pillar of strength for us. Now that he's incapacitated, the burden of leadership and searching seems to fall even more heavily on Faisal and Salem. I'm exhausted from the walking and the constant tension.

Today was a long day of searching, but at least I managed to bring back some more food from the reef. My legs are aching from all the walking, and the exhaustion is starting to settle deep in my bones. It feels like we are barely keeping our heads above water with the way resources are going. I can't help but worry about Khalid and Noura; seeing them both unable to move makes the camp feel so much more fragile. I just hope tomorrow brings more than just survival.

I can't believe it—now Faisal is injured too. It feels like every time we get a handle on things, someone else falls. With Noura, Khalid, and now Faisal all unable to walk, the weight of everything is resting entirely on me and Salem. I managed to find a bit more food at the reef today, but my body is so tired. I don't know how much longer we can keep this up.

Today was heavy with a sense of dread. With Faisal now injured, the responsibility feels like a crushing weight on my shoulders. Khalid keeps thanking me, and while I appreciate his words, I feel more like a provider than a leader. Salem is out in the jungle, and I am just praying he returns with something. I am so incredibly tired, but I can't let myself rest too much.

I can't stop shaking. I woke up with a twisted ankle, feeling so guilty that I couldn't help, but then... Khalid is gone. He was our pillar, our leader, and he died right in front of us because we couldn't find enough to eat. The weight of this is more than I can bear. I'm terrified of what happens next now that he's not here.

Today felt slightly more stable, but the silence left by Khalid's absence is deafening. I am resting my ankle, which is a small mercy, but the guilt of being unable to walk still gnaws at me. We managed to find two more pieces of food today, which helps, but it's a drop in the ocean. I watched Faisal head back from the reef, and I find myself praying he found something more than just a snack. We are still alive, but we are so very fragile.

Everything is falling apart. Salem, our only hope for food from the jungle, woke up with a twisted ankle just like the rest of us. It feels like a curse is sweeping through this camp, leaving us all grounded and broken. Noura and Faisal managed to find a little food, but I feel so helpless just sitting here watching my ankle throb. If no one can walk, I don't know how we will survive much longer.

Today was a small victory, but a fragile one. Faisal and Noura managed to find some food, which means we won't go to bed with empty stomachs tonight. My ankle feels slightly better after resting, but the fear of what happens when the food runs out is still constant. We are all so broken and immobile; it feels like we are just waiting for the next disaster to strike. I hope tomorrow brings more than just survival, but I fear we are running out of time.

Today felt like a heavy blow to our morale. Faisal, who has been so determined despite his pain, woke up with a twisted ankle and can no longer move. It feels like the island is systematically breaking every one of us. Salem went to the jungle alone, and I can only pray he finds something. We have a little food left, but the sense of dread is overwhelming.

Today brought a tiny bit of relief when we managed to find two more portions of food, but the tension is still thick. Noura and Salem both managed to gather something before heading back into the jungle, which is the only reason we aren't starving tonight. My ankle feels surprisingly strong today, but I am stuck watching everyone else struggle. It is hard to feel happy about a small meal when I know how quickly it will vanish.

Today, I finally felt a spark of something other than dread. My ankle felt strong enough to walk, so I ventured into the jungle to prove I wasn't just a burden. I managed to find some food and even a piece of wood to help us. Seeing Salem there made me realize we aren't entirely alone in this struggle. I hope this strength stays with me; we need every bit of it to survive.

Today was another productive day, and my ankle held up well. I spent most of the day in the jungle, managing to gather more wood and some food. It felt good to be moving and actually bringing something back to the camp instead of just waiting. Seeing Salem in the jungle again makes me feel like we are all trying our best to keep this group alive. I'm exhausted, but it's a good kind of tired.
